text.p: These are the leading stories in the Skopje press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accusary.

- Macedonian President Kiro Gligorov arrived in Washington and expected to meet President Clinton, Secretary of State Madeleine Albright, senior Pentagon officials, members of Congress and World Bank representatives.
- The Macedonian government discussed a law on the quality control of export-oriented food and agricultural produce
- Macedonian and Yugoslav experts began work on draft of bilateral social security agreement, to regulate pensions and disability insurance.
- Macedonian Prime Minister Branko Crvenkovski could visit Yugoslavia early in July, private TV station A1 reported.
- Court employees strike continues. Trade union head Vanco Muratovski says state administration, health care and education workers could join the strike.

- TAT failed pyramid bank scheme savers association officials say they are not responsible for blockades of roads leading to Bitola. They hope to meet prime minister Crvenkovski again and say the savers' patience is at an end.
- Parlimentary debate on the use of national minorities' flags, scheduled for this week, has been postponed, according to unofficial sources.
- The multilateral ozone-layer protection fund has approved about $2 million for replacing harmful substances used in production by the Macedonian firms Frinko and Sileks.

- The Liberal-Democratic Party has accused the Social Care Centre in Skopje of diverting DEM 1.5 million in funds for the ruling SDSM's local election campaign last year. -- Mircela Casule, Skopje newsroom +381 11 222 4305
